carlos_customer: Hey folks, we rolled out the new quant profile "safe_int8_alpha" across our dedicated cluster (dc-east-2) last night and woke up to p95 spikes. p50 stayed ~95ms but p95 ~610ms and p99 ~1.05s. Also noticed occasional gibberish at the end of responses. Sample request id: req_x9b7. Model: redwood-70b-alpha. Any immediate ideas?

olivia_support: sorry about that Carlos. Do you have the exact deploy time and whether any auto-scaling or batch settings changed around the same time?

carlos_customer: deploy at 2026-07-14T22:03:00Z. No scaling changes, concurrency steady at 6, sequence lengths are around 400-600 tokens for this workload. We did enable quant_profile=safe_int8_alpha via Console → Deployments → Runtime Overrides.

olivia_support: copying. I'm going to run a probe against your endpoint with similar concurrency, will post logs.

ops-bot: [2026-07-14T22:05:12Z] auto-monitor: p95_alert triggered for dc-east-2 (p95=612ms)

olivia_support (probe): ran 6 parallel requests for ~2 minutes, captured timings and a snippet of kernel debug.

olivia_support (probe logs): ```
[2026-07-15T02:06:45Z] req=req_x9b7 worker=w-12 quant_profile=safe_int8_alpha kernel_flow=int8->fp32_dequant
[2026-07-15T02:06:45Z] req=req_x9b7 kv_cache_hit=false kv_fetch=9.6ms memcpy=6.1ms
[2026-07-15T02:06:45Z] worker=w-12 layer=attn dequantize_time=10.7ms requantize_time=7.2ms
[2026-07-15T02:06:45Z] worker=w-12 kernel_selector=compatible_fp8_missing -> fallback_generic
```
Looks like several ops are taking dequant/requant time and kernel selector chose a fallback codepath because the node's driver/kernel set lacks fp8/native int8 operators.

mike_runtime: jumping in. Two things to consider: (A) "safe_int8_alpha" appears to use asymmetric scale buckets that our older kernels can't process in-place, so we force out-of-place dequant/requant for KV updates; (B) at seq len ~500 the KV copy cost increases and the per-token overhead ramps tail latency. This matches the p95/p99 pattern you're seeing.

lena_ml: from the ML side, the profile was calibrated on a mixed-prod sample but not specifically for seq lengths >400 or for the exact weight layout of redwood-70b-alpha. The profile tries to compress tails which can create many small-scale clusters and hurt runtime locality. That also explains occasional quality artifacts.

olivia_support: immediate mitigation options (fast to slow):
- Option 1 (fastest): roll back runtime profile to fp16_default on dc-east-2. Zero model changes, immediate latency fix.
- Option 2: revert to previous int8 profile "int8_prod_v1" which we know works well on this infra. Lower risk but might miss some cost savings.
- Option 3: pin requests to a node-pool that has fp8/int8 native kernels (requires infra assist).
- Option 4: run a dedicated calibration pass using your corpus + our calibration harness and produce a node-compatible profile.

carlos_customer: we prefer an immediate rollback to keep SLAs intact. Please proceed with rollback and keep me posted. Also we need a postmortem of why this profile slipped past the gate.

olivia_support: initiating rollback now. Creating an override route to send traffic to fp16 variant while we monitor.

ops-bot: [2026-07-15T02:12:03Z] deploy: rollback started user=olivia_support target=dc-east-2 change="quant_profile:safe_int8_alpha -> fp16_default" rollout_id=roll-10214

olivia_support (monitoring): after override p95 dropped to 138ms, p99=240ms within ~5m. Can you validate from your side @carlos_customer?

carlos_customer: confirmed p95 ~140ms and outputs look normal. Thanks for the quick rollback.

mike_runtime: root cause sketch for follow-up: profile "safe_int8_alpha" exposes quant scales that interact poorly with our current KV memory layout on older CUDA/driver combos; kernel_selector can't pick the in-place int8 kernels and triggers a generic fallback that performs expensive copies + dequant ops per attention step. The cost per call is small but accumulates at p95/p99. Also the calibration test lacked a specific tail-latency gate.

lena_ml: ML follow-ups:
- We'll create an "infra-aware" quantization step that checks node kernel capabilities before promoting a profile.
- Add a latency-focused calibration metric (p95 on a realistic seq-length distribution) to the promotion CI.

mike_runtime: infra/ops follow-ups:
- Add a runtime metric that reports "fallback_generic" kernel invocations per deployment; hook into alerts so support sees it automatically. (P0)
- Add a canary rule that blocks promotion of new quant profiles to clusters where kernel capability is unknown. (P1)

olivia_support: customer-facing follow-ups:
- We rolled you back to fp16_default at 2026-07-15T02:12:03Z.
- If you want to try int8 again, we can run a calibration using your corpus on a small canary pool first.
- Feature request noted: add "last quant profile change" timestamp and diff in the deployment UI.

carlos_customer: please add me to the calibration run and keep us in the loop. Also can you provide a short blameless postmortem once internal actions are assigned?

olivia_support: will do. Filing follow-ups now and adding you to the calibration invite. Thanks for the quick signal and patience. :heart:

mike_runtime (tracking): filing internal ticket RUNTIME-6110 "safe_int8_alpha causes fallback_generic kernel usage on older nodes -> p95 regressions". Attaching logs and sample profile.

lena_ml (tracking): filing ML ticket ML-2982 "add p95 gate to quant profile promotion + infra-aware profiles".

olivia_support: closing this support escalation for now; reopen if you see any new tail spikes.

carlos_customer: closing on our side too. Appreciate the fast response and rollback.

(reacts: :white_check_mark:, :folded_hands:)
